turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry we're late. Car park was a nightmare, two wrong turns, and my sister had a stroke last year so I go to pieces about hospitals.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're alright, you're still on the list. That sort of family history would unsettle anyone. Sit yourself down.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. So what actually brought you in today?
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm. I woke up and one side of my face has drooped.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which side is it?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): The left. I can't close the eye properly and I can't whistle. Tried in the mirror, nothing.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did you first notice?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): This morning, about seven, when I got up.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the ear before it started?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Left ear, yes. I was going to say three days, no, sorry, it was just yesterday.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Still sore now?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit, yeah. Easier than yesterday.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the arm or the leg, or trouble getting your words out?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Grip's normal, legs are fine, talking's fine. Just feels weird round the mouth.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Felt hot or shivery?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No temperature.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lost any weight without trying?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm, I don't weigh myself. Maybe a pound, maybe I haven't. I couldn't say.
[SEG0019] person_3 (NURSE): Sorry, observations. Blood pressure 138 over 84, pulse 76. And the list says amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll trust the blood pressure. The dose is wrong though, I take ten milligrams, not five.
[SEG0021] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The box at home says ten. Little white ones.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, we leave the dose unsettled. You do have high blood pressure, and you're taking that?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, high blood pressure, for years. I just take what's in the box.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eyebrows up for me, as high as you can.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Left one won't move. Is this a stroke? My sister's started in the face, they told us.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me think it out. Forehead's weak on the left as well. A stroke up in the brain usually spares the forehead, so this looks more like the nerve to the face.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): The nerve, not the brain? How sure are you, honestly?
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not sure enough to call it final. Working idea only. Now shut your eyes tight.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I can't. Left stays open a crack, I can feel the air.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, incomplete closure of the left eye, and the left corner of the mouth barely lifts when you smile.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): And not whistling, that counts, yes? Is it permanent? I'm a receptionist, I live on the phone.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): It counts, yes. Push both arms up against my hands.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arm strength is normal both sides. Speech is clear, I'm not hearing any slurring.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): So do you think it's Bell's palsy? A girl at work had that. Will my voice sound drunk?
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Working impression is a left sided Bell's palsy. Provisional. The facial nerve gets inflamed, often after something viral and mild, and the ear pain yesterday fits.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Does it come back? I need weeks or days or what. I can't be off the desk forever.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Usually weeks, sometimes a few months. I can't date your recovery today.
[SEG0040] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She hardly slept, doctor, pacing half the night.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): I didn't sleep, no. If it drops further this afternoon, do I come straight back?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll cover that. Steroid first. Prednisolone, twenty five milligrams, no, I want fifty milligrams, once a day, by mouth, for ten days.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Fifty? I'll be manic, won't I, or huge? People online say awful things about steroids.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ten days is short. Take it in the morning with some food. It can bother the stomach or your sleep. It won't really put weight on you in that time.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): The eye feels dry and scratchy already. What if it gets scratched for good?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it can't close, the surface dries. Use hypromellose drops, every two hours through the day while you're awake.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Hypomellose? And at night, do I just leave it open?
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hypromellose, that's the one. At night, tape the eyelid shut. A plain eye ointment from the chemist as well if they've got it.
[SEG0049] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll do the tape. We've got some micropore.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): What if I still need a scan? My sister had one the same afternoon. I'm frightened you'll miss a stroke.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't scan you today, forehead's involved and the arms and speech are clear. If the eye goes red or the vision blurs, come straight back or go to eye casualty. If an arm weakens or the speech changes, that's A&E, don't sit on it. Otherwise I'll see you here in one week.
[SEG0052] person_1 (PATIENT): Ok. And tonight, five milligrams or ten? I'm not guessing wrong with the blood pressure tablet.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take the dose printed on your box. We are not changing it off a mismatched list. Questions are fine, I'll see you in a week.

spec.situation: Person woke with one side of the face drooping, cannot close the eye, cannot whistle; no arm weakness, no speech problem, ear pain a day before; doctor examines and starts steroids, eye care explained.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
